topics.title: 课程作业
topics.summary: 国王学院不禁止 AI，但每项考核允许的程度由考核说明按四个建议等级设定：Minimal（拼写语法检查、自动转写）、Limited/selective（限定任务）、Open（无具体限制但须记录关键步骤）、Embedded（AI 是任务组成部分）。根据《学术不端政策》，把 AI 输出复制进提交物是不恰当的，作品必须是学生本人的；不确定时应询问。
topics.scope: 四级框架与学术不端政策第 4.2–4.5 节。

claims.text: King's College London suggests four broad levels of generative AI use in assessment that programme and module leaders may adjust to each assessment: Minimal (routine tools such as auto transcription, spell and grammar checkers), Limited/selective (clearly delineated tasks as allowed), Open (no specific restrictions but key stages and tools must be tracked) and Embedded (AI use is a focal part of the assessment). The levels are a framework for the actual assessment brief, not an automatic university-wide permission, and verbatim use of generated content without acknowledgement is never appropriate.

claims.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy states that using generative AI tools to produce output that is then copied as part of a submission is not appropriate, that any work submitted must genuinely demonstrate the student's own work, skills and knowledge and follow the assessment guidelines, and that generative AI writing programmes are third-party technologies to be used only in accordance with College guidance. The King's guidance adds that submitting AI-generated text as one's own without written departmental permission is considered misconduct (third-party involvement or text manipulation) where it gives undue advantage or interferes with assessment of the student's own understanding. A written permission or acknowledgement does not by itself make substantive AI content creation acceptable.

evidence.quote: However, the use of generative AI tools to produce output which is then copied as part of a submission is not appropriate. Prudent, ethical and constructive use of tools is increasingly likely to form part of the production of assessed work.
evidence.title: Academic Misconduct Policy (effective 1 September 2023; next review September 2026)

topics.title: 披露声明
topics.summary: 学生须在课程作业的参考文献处附声明，说明生成式 AI 的使用情况（考核说明另有措辞的除外）：要么声明没有任何部分由 AI 生成（使用语法和拼写检查与此一致），要么声明部分内容有 AI 参与且符合考核说明的可接受范围，并写明工具及用途。AI 不作为权威来源引用。博士生须在 RD2 表格中选择两种 AI 声明之一。
topics.scope: 课程作业声明与 RD2 表格。

claims.text: King's College London does not require students to cite generative AI as an authoritative source in the reference list, but it requires students to acknowledge any use of generative AI tools in coursework by including a declaration statement with their references. Unless the assessment brief gives other wording, students append either a declaration that no part of the submission was generated by AI software (English grammar and spell checking is consistent with this statement) or a declaration that parts of the submission have AI contributions within the acceptable use specified in the brief, naming the tools and how they were used.

evidence.quote: King’s College London, unlike some other universities, does not require students to reference generative AI as an authoritative source in the reference list for much the same reason you would not be expected to cite a search engine, a student essay website or be over-dependent on synoptic, secondary source material.

topics.statusLabel: 不得输入个人或他人内容
topics.summary: 即使国王学院的 Copilot 有商业数据保护，学生也不应向任何 AI 平台输入个人数据、敏感信息或他人创作的内容。博士生在上传研究项目任何部分前，须与导师团队讨论保密、版权、数据保护和伦理问题并取得书面批准。教职员工未经明确许可不得把学生作品或信息上传到 AI 工具。
topics.scope: 学生指引、博士上传审批与评分指引。

claims.text: King's College London states that its Enterprise licence means Copilot use comes with commercial data protection, making it a more secure alternative to other generative AI tools. claims.text: King's College London permits doctoral students to use generative AI tools in an assistive role in thesis writing, to clarify their own writing and avoid misrepresenting their meaning; this can include rewriting, rephrasing or paraphrasing parts of the thesis. evidence.quote: Yes, students are permitted to make use of generative AI tools in their thesis writing processes. However, where a student's use of generative AI tools in their thesis writing exceeds the circumstances permitted by this guidance, they will risk breaching the Academic Misconduct Policy.

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与纪律程序
additionalTopics.summary: 不当且未注明的 AI 使用可构成学术不端，但不规范的学术做法（如引用不完整）不属于不端。案件通常从非正式的学术诚信会议开始，学生可能被要求解释作品，但无义务给出特定回答。第一阶段处罚可在书面通知后 10 个工作日内提出异议；不端委员会决定可在 10 个工作日内基于有限理由上诉。处理结果从警告、限分重交到停学或开除不等。国王学院未启用 Turnitin 的 AI 检测百分比，但相似性检查仍在使用。

claims.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy distinguishes poor academic practice from academic misconduct: an ASB Chair may decide a concern is an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice (for example incomplete citation), which is not misconduct; the student receives feedback and the work is marked against the criteria. Blatant, extensive or careless failures are excluded from this category.

evidence.quote: Once the ASB Chair (or their nominee) has reviewed the information available, they may decide that the concern relates to poor academic practice and that no academic misconduct has occurred. Poor academic practice involves an unintentional misunderstanding of scholarly practice. Examples include when sources are acknowledged to some extent, but citation is inadequate or incomplete. It does not include when the failure to adhere to scholarly practice is blatant, extensive or results from a lack of effort. Poor academic practice is not a form of academic misconduct.

claims.text: Under King's Academic Misconduct Policy, a suspected case normally goes first to a Stage One Academic Integrity Meeting (AIM) with two staff members. The AIM is not a hearing and should be informal, supportive and exploratory; where authorship or third-party involvement is in doubt the student may be asked to explain their answers, ideas or references, but must not be pressured or obliged to give specific responses and may respond in writing instead. Staff share their notes, and the student may add information, normally within 5 working days. Possible Stage One outcomes are no concern, poor academic practice, a local educative or restorative outcome, or referral to a Stage Two Misconduct Committee.

claims.text: King's Academic Misconduct Policy provides two different review routes with different start points. Where a Stage One AIM finds misconduct and applies a local penalty (Outcome 3), the student may send a contestation in writing to Student Conduct & Appeals within 10 working days from the date of written notification of the Stage One outcome. A Stage Two Misconduct Committee decision may be appealed, on the grounds of new evidence or significant procedural error, by submitting a Misconduct Appeal Form within 10 working days of the date of the Misconduct Committee outcome. Possible outcomes range from educative measures such as a formal warning or capped resubmission to punitive outcomes up to suspension or expulsion; AI use does not carry an automatic penalty.

additionalTopics.title: 教学与课程指引
additionalTopics.summary: 伦敦国王学院支持审慎使用生成式 AI，并愿意根据需求和学科差异改进教学、考核与反馈实践。关于 AI 辅助评分与反馈的机构指引（2025年7月）强调，审阅和评估学生作业应主要由人工进行，且必须有人工监督以确保准确性和适切性。教师不应使用 GenAI 工具来检测学生的 AI 使用情况，因为此类工具极不可靠。未经明确同意、许可与深思熟虑，工作人员绝不应将学生作业或个人信息上传至任何 AI 系统或 GenAI 工具；进行 AI 辅助反馈和评分时，应使用学校批准或支持的大学 GenAI 工具。该指引规范教职人员的评分与数据处理实践，并非针对学生的课程使用许可。
additionalTopics.scope: 背景定义与 AI 辅助评分及反馈指引（2025年7月）；考核演进、教工数据处理与检测工具立场。

claims.text: King's guidance for AI-assisted marking and feedback (July 2025) says staff should never upload student work to any AI system without explicit consent and forethought, should not include student details or upload work into any GenAI tool without explicit permission, should use approved or supported university GenAI tools, and should keep reading and assessing student work primarily human with human oversight. Staff should not use GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI. This guidance governs staff marking and data handling; it is not a rule about students' own AI use.
